title: Introduce credentialless tenant bootstrap operator + Helm preflight policy checks
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds credentialless tenant bootstrap operator + Helm preflight policy checks to improve private installer idempotency and reduce manual RBAC steps for air-gapped/private deployments. Includes Terraform module updates and a rollback playbook.
description: Motivation: Private deployments require repeated, safe onboarding of tenant control-plane components without exposing long-lived credentials. This PR adds a credentialless tenant bootstrap operator that performs ephemeral workload identity exchanges (K8s ServiceAccount token + short-lived bootstrap grants) and an accompanying Helm preflight policy-check step that verifies RBAC templates, policy bundles, and required KMS secrets before applying charts. The goal is to reduce manual steps for customers using the private installer (VPC/on-prem) and to make automated upgrades and rollback safer. Summary of changes (high level): - New controller: installer/boot/credentialless-operator (scaffold, controllers, admission helpers) - Helm preflight check: helm/preflight/policy-checker (validates policy bundles, checks required KMS/HSM keys, and cross-checks tenant isolation constraints) - Terraform: modules/tenant_bootstrap enhancements to support bootstrap tokens and conditional outputs for air-gapped flows - Helm charts: charts/private/values.schema.yaml and charts/private/templates/rbac-helpers.yaml updated to consume ephemeral grants - Rollback playbook: playbooks/rollback/tenant-rbac-rollback.md with stepwise rollback & verification steps - Docs: docs/private/bootstrapping.md and quickstart snippets added - Tests: tests/integration/bootstrap_e2e.sh and unit tests for operator reconciliation Why this approach: Using a short-lived bootstrap grant mitigates the need to ship secrets in configmaps or store long-lived service principal keys in TF state. The preflight policy checks prevent failed installs due to missing KMS keys or mis-scoped RBAC templates. Checklist: - [x] Operator scaffold and controller reconciliation loop - [x] Helm preflight checker and schema validation - [x] Terraform module changes and backward-compatible outputs - [x] Playbook and docs updated - [x] Integration tests and smoke tests - [x] Security review and threat model notes Related work: ENG-4213 (tenant bootstrap redesign), ENG-4298 (helm preflight architecture), SUP-214 (support case: failed private installs due to missing KMS keys). Migration notes: Existing installs will continue to work; new installs can opt into credentialless mode via values.privateInstaller.bootstrap.mode=credentialless. There is an optional migration helper that emits a one-time ephemeral grant and updates TF outputs; it is documented in docs/private/bootstrapping.md.

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Please ensure the operator falls back to the existing TF-based bootstrap when running in legacy mode. I hit a race in the e2e where TF outputs weren't present yet.
Aisha Patel (author): Added a conditional check and an explicit wait in the operator when values.legacyFallback=true. Also added a logging note so operators can see the fallback path.
Lina Zhao: Security review: the ephemeral grant exchange logic looks solid but we need an audit trail for grant issuance. Can we emit an event and wire it to audit logs?
Aisha Patel (author): Added audit event emission on grant creation and included a sample AuditSink config in docs. Also added metadata to the TF output to link to the grant request id.
Kenji Sato: Helm preflight is great. Suggest adding a --skip-policy flag for lab installs and explicitly documenting the consequences.
Aisha Patel (author): Added --skip-policy to the preflight CLI and documented it; clarified that skipping is only recommended for dev/lab environments.
